The slides were examined using a Zeiss fluorescent microscope.

Various tissue samples were used, including breast, spleen, colon, kidney, uterus, lung, and heart. The sample slides were rehydrated in a series of washes: xylene, 100% ethanol, 95% ethanol, diH20, and PBS.

Immunohistochemistry was performed using a Super Sensitive Detection System kit (Biogenex, San Ramon, CA). The slides were treated with 3% H202 and Power Block. Incubation for one hour with CAR-1 antibody at 1:100 followed. The slides were then incubated with Superblock for 20 min, treated with Poly-HRP, and treated with AEC substrate until the slides were sufficiently stained, between 5-40 min. After rinsing with PBS, they were treated with Hematoxylin, rinsed with tap water, and dipped in 10% ammonium water for, rinsed with tap water, and finally Supermounted.
From the Western blot probed with the CAR-1 C-terminal antibody, the size of CAR-1 was determined to be approximately 64 kD (Fig. 2).
Fig. 2 CAR-1 Western blot; at 1:20,000; size 64kD

The immunocytochemistry slides were stained with DAPI to visualize DNA and CAR-1 protein was visualized as a CAR-1-GFP fusion. For all samples, CAR-1-GFP fluorescence occurred outside the nucleus, in the cytoplasm, indicating cytoplasmic localization of CAR-1. The normal HFS cells exhibited diffuse CAR-1-GFP fluorescence (Fig. 3).
Fig. 3 HFS Cells (left) and tumor cells from 21MT (right)

More importantly, numerous bright green speckles were seen in almost all the cells. These speckles are purported to be the formation of macromolecular structures, similar to those seen associated with BRCA-1.¹,² In contrast, the tumor cell (21MT) slides produced a distinct network of GFP fluorescence with a spidery texture and very few speckles could be found in the cells (Fig. 3).

The immunohistochemistry slides contained a blue nuclear staining and a brick red CAR-1 protein staining. The results of the normal tissues indicated distinct CAR-1 staining predominantly targeted around ductal structures, suggesting CAR-1 localization specific for ductal tissue. Lung, heart, and uterus (Fig. 4) samples appeared to exhibit CAR-1 staining concentrated at specific structures. Spleen samples showed weak and diffuse CAR-1 staining throughout (Fig. 4).
Fig. 4 (Clockwise from top left) Lung, heart, uterus and spleen samples
In normal breast tissue, CAR-1 staining was very distinct, targeting the epithelial cells lining the ductal structures (Fig. 5).
Fig. 5 Staining in normal breast tissue (left) and breast fiboradenoma tissue (right)

Though the ductal structures in breast fibroadenoma tissue are compressed, staining was still specific (Fig. 5). Staining in the uterus and kidney (Fig. 7), both ductal tissues, were especially concentrated around ductal structures.
